gate_objections: part 7 (pages 141-165): The TEMPERAMENT NOTE lists which questions are asked at each age band (3-5, 6-11, 12-23, 24-35 and 36-47 months). The CHILD CARE NOTE does the same for 0-11 months, 12-23 months, 2-3 years, 4-5 years and 6-11 years. Both are 'ask only if' gates, and the inventory has no `conditions` entry on any TMP or CAR question for them. The scope entries mark the notes 'in', but no question carries the age restriction. Examples: TMP-Q13A and TMP-Q21A are age-banded, and CAR-Q1H and CAR-Q8 are asked only for certain ages.

part 7 (pages 141-165): CAR-Q1J1 carries a mined check summing the weekly hours of CAR-Q1B1 through CAR-Q1J1 against 168. Its `hint` is written in a mix of Spanish and French ('El total de horas por semana ... ne peut pas dépasser ... revisez'), while the questionnaire is English and `source_language` is 'en'. The hint must be in the source language. The predicate also adds fields that are skipped or unanswered by design, since many of the hour questions are conditional and the child may not use that arrangement, so it needs to handle missing values.

part 10 (pages 192-203): Question 22: the options are printed with codes 01–10, but the inventory gives them values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 and 512. The printed codes survive only inside the label text. Item 03 (hearing impairment) has value 4, item 05 (learning disability) has value 16, and item 10 (some other type of problem) has value 512. Use the printed codes 1–10 as the option values.

part 13 (pages 223-237): Q26a/26b: the source prints these two rows without a question number or stem. The inventory invents ids '26a' and '26b' and gives them no stem. 'source_id exactly as printed' is not met, and the stem is missing from the text.

part 13 (pages 223-237): Q27 and Q28 availability/rating codes: the source prints codes 01-24 (27) and 01-90 (28), and the inventory keeps them as the printed values. For Q27 the 'No' cell is printed as 'O-->' beside the code, which implies a jump past the days field. The inventory instead recorded the days field as a condition on 'Yes' and no jump, so the 'O-->' arrows are not recorded as routing, and the Q27 availability codes are renumbered 1/2 instead of the printed 01/02, 03/04 and so on. Printed codes should be kept.
part 13 (pages 223-237): Q27: 'No -->' arrows for each row (a to l) are routing instructions printed in the source; there is no jump for any of them (12 missing).

part 13 (pages 223-237): Q32 checks: the mined 'at this school <= total' checks are marked invented true, which is fine, but the predicates use '@[32b]' for years, which is a different question from the months field. This is acceptable only if the pairs are modelled as two questions. The source prints each row as ONE question with two boxes (codes 01/02 etc.), so splitting into separate years/months questions changes the structure and adds ids not printed in the source.
part 13 (pages 223-237): TWOWK-Q4 check hint is written in Spanish while the source is English; the hint should be in the questionnaire language.

part 13 (pages 223-237): TCH-C2 jump: the source target 'TCH-I3' is not in the part, which is allowed. But the TCH-C2 jump to TCH-Q2 for 'OTHERWISE' is fine. HHLD-Q6 does not appear in the part, which is allowed. However, HHLD-Q5 is flagged 'OTHER ---> GO TO HHLD-Q6', which is recorded; OK.

part 13 (pages 223-237): UTIL-Q2 is modelled as one multiple-choice question with an invented bitmask code set. The source prints ten category items with no codes, and the follow-up 'RESPONSE >0 IN a), c), or d)' implies a numeric count per category. The inventory's modelling as a checkbox is not what the source prints.

part 13 (pages 223-237): Scope: the inventory lists 'THANK YOU FOR COMPLETING...' as in, though it is not a question. More importantly, the Q35 'Do you have any comments about this survey?' is given an invented id '35'; the source prints no number.

part 13 (pages 223-237): External inputs: the inventory adds 'COLLECTION_PERIOD', 'IN_SCHOOL', 'GRADE' and 'AGE' as external questions with invented option codes. 'AGE' etc. are plausible, but KCON-Q1A/Q1B conditions test an invented variable whose codes were made up. It is better to record the note as given.
